description: We are a six-member student team from Myanmar integrating software engineering, AI, scientific research, UX design, and storytelling into a single unit. We work together across the entire lifecycle—from data architecture to user experience—to build transparent, evidence-first technology that turns complex space data into functional, impact-driven products.
summary: IGNIS is an evidence-first fire-safety intelligence tool for human spaceflight. Fire behaves differently in microgravity, and guessing is dangerous — so IGNIS never predicts. Instead, it retrieves verified NASA solid-material flammability experiments (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I–VI, USML-1) and shows what actually happened: the observed outcome, the exact test conditions, and a verbatim quote with a page-level citation from the original NASA report. Describe a material and environment, and IGNIS returns the closest documented experiments — 31 verified runs across 8 NASA campaigns, spanning 16.4–31% oxygen and 54–101 kPa — and makes every evidence gap visible instead of papering over it. Every published record was verified by a named human reviewer against the source document, and a built-in 60-second case lets anyone tamper with a value and watch IGNIS refuse what the record doesn't support.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

IGNIS answers one question: "What has NASA actually observed when material X burns in conditions Y?" A user describes a scenario in plain language or picks a preset (cabin wall, crew clothing, cable insulation). IGNIS retrieves the matching flight experiments from its verified catalog and presents each one as an evidence card: material, oxygen %, pressure, airflow, observed outcome (sustained / extinguished / transitioned / did not ignite), and a verbatim quotation with page, table, or figure locator linking straight to the NASA source PDF. Where conditions changed mid-test (e.g., airflow stepped 10→2.2 cm/s), the record stores both values rather than flattening them. Where no experiment exists, IGNIS says so — the Gap Radar shows what has not been tested, because in fire safety an honest "no data" is safer than a confident guess.

HOW IT'S BUILT

React 18 + TypeScript + Vite frontend; Supabase Postgres with row-level security; Vercel serverless API; Zod validation on every boundary; 317 automated tests plus a live-verification suite (npm run verify:live) that fails if any published value ever differs from its NASA source. Natural-language scenario parsing uses an LLM (Groq, with Gemini fallback) — but the LLM only maps words to filter parameters; it never generates, estimates, or embellishes evidence. The claim-checker behind the 60-second case is fully deterministic, no LLM involved.

DATA INTEGRITY — OUR CORE DESIGN FACTOR

Publication requires a named human reviewer. Drafts are invisible to the public by database policy, not convention. Every populated field carries a quote and locator; missing values stay null. A fixtures file pins all 31 cards to their source values in CI. Mid-event, we caught edited values on 12 published cards, reverted them to drafts, re-verified each against the NASA PDFs, and republished — the guard suite now makes that class of error impossible to ship silently.

IMPACT AND USERS

For professors, students, and aerospace researchers and engineers, IGNIS turns scattered NTRS PDFs into a queryable, citable evidence base — while modeling what trustworthy AI-adjacent tooling should look like: retrieval with receipts, visible gaps, and zero invented numbers.

CREATIVITY

Most teams build predictors. We built the opposite — a system whose refusal to predict is the feature. The 60-second case invites judges to try to make IGNIS lie, live.
